purpose: Candidate V2 base style delta for object-first/non-human-first card art. This file does NOT duplicate the D4 rendering language - it references global_style_v1.json's existing 'prompt' field as the base rendering style (read-only) and layers V2-specific policy on top. V1 is never modified by this file. A V2-capable compiler (not yet built - see the handoff's 'not yet built' section) would read this file in addition to global_style_v1.json, in place of the V1-only path.
base_style_conflict_disclosure_SUPERSEDE: HISTORICAL RECORD ONLY, no longer the active mechanism - kept for audit trail. The 2026-09-25 compiler checkpoint (commit 3175b77) reused global_style_v1.json's 'prompt' field verbatim plus an override clause to neutralize its human/character-oriented language ('expressive faces', 'bright, appealing eyes', 'elegant stylized anatomy', 'expressive but mature character design', 'clean character silhouettes', a focal-hierarchy tier naming 'supporting people'). This checkpoint (the final zero-cost gate) replaced that patch-over approach with v2_native_style below, an actual human-language-free base style written for V2, now explicitly authorized. global_screen_policy was already excluded (not reused) as of 3175b77 for the same reason (its 'Recognition must come from the person...' clause); this checkpoint replaces that omission with a real, positive V2 screen policy (screen_policy_v2 below) rather than leaving screens covered only by the brief non_human_protagonist_policy line.
base_style_override_clause_SUPERSEDED: HISTORICAL RECORD ONLY. No longer inserted into compiled prompts as of the 2026-09-25 final zero-cost gate checkpoint - superseded by v2_native_style, which does not require an override clause because it never contains character/face/anatomy language in the first place. Original text: "The character-rendering, face, eye, and anatomy language above describes the illustration's linework and shading quality only, not a mandate to include a human character. For this card, that rendering quality must be applied entirely to the non-human protagonist, object, animal, or environment described below - no human character, face, or body may be composed into this scene, including as supporting background people."
v2_native_style: Create a premium full-art Japanese-inspired special illustration for a real-world hobby, with a non-human protagonist (an object, animal, environment, machine, food, miniature, or abstract system - never a human character). This must be unmistakably illustrated artwork, not photography. The rendering language should feel like polished contemporary Japanese commercial illustration: clean confident linework, refined cel shading, soft painted gradients, crisp readable silhouettes, rich but controlled color, luminous highlights, polished finish, and tactile, believable material detail (metal, wood, fabric, water, glass, fur, or whatever the protagonist is made of). However, do NOT compose this as an ordinary static catalog or product shot, and do NOT simply show the hobby's objects sitting inertly with no dramatic moment. Instead, compose the scene as an ICONIC SPECIAL-ILLUSTRATION MOMENT: a rare full-art key visual with one unforgettable focal moment, a strong hero object or hero interaction, dynamic composition, visual flow toward the hobby's defining detail, foreground elements that create depth and energy, supporting background shapes that serve the main subject, directional environmental movement, clear visual rhythm, a memorable silhouette, a strong palette identity, and a sense of "this is the moment". The central subject should dominate the composition. Use strong focal hierarchy: (1) the hero moment, (2) the hobby-defining object or environmental detail, (3) supporting environment or secondary objects, (4) a small delightful detail. Do not give equal visual importance to every object or environmental element in the scene, and do not spread attention evenly across the entire image. Avoid ordinary documentary composition and a cluttered scene with no clear single hero element - instead stage a single emotional or atmospheric peak. Use clean, dynamic linework, polished shading, a bright harmonious palette, subtle rim light, sparkling highlights and small glints where semantically appropriate, stylized steam/wind/dust/paper movement where appropriate, graphic color accents, lively perspective, mild perspective exaggeration, foreground framing elements, and a strong diagonal or circular visual flow when helpful - these effects should create excitement and collectibility, and must NOT turn the scene into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself requires it. Default emotional atmosphere: joyful, engaging, optimistic, energetic, curious, triumphant, exciting, inviting, aspirational; serious subjects may use tension, fascination, determination, revelation, or intellectual excitement, but should not become gloomy, depressing, muted, solemn, or dark prestige-TV realism. Prefer clean, colorful palettes, warm/cool contrast, saturated but controlled hues, a visually memorable palette identity, luminous accents, and attractive color separation between hero and background; avoid beige lifestyle palettes, muddy brown-heavy grading, monochrome editorial restraint, Western cinematic desaturation, and corporate muted color schemes. The artwork must be full-bleed and edge-to-edge. Do NOT draw a card border, white border, rounded frame, decorative frame, printed-paper edge, faux card shell, TCG layout, title bar, stats box, logo badge, corner emblem, rarity symbol, or UI panel - the application adds any card UI later; the generated image itself must be pure artwork. Do NOT render photography, stock photo, DSLR realism, movie-still, photo bokeh, lens blur, Western magazine editorial art, flat corporate illustration, New Yorker-like restrained editorial illustration, Western concept art, gritty fantasy splash art, dark prestige-TV look, generic AI-anime portrait, chibi, preschool cartoon, excessive unrelated magic, fantasy weapons unrelated to the hobby, supernatural aura, card frame, trading-card UI, readable logo/title text, franchise characters, or recognizable franchise-specific motifs. Semantic fidelity remains mandatory - do not sacrifice hobby correctness to achieve style.
v2_native_style_note: Written this checkpoint (2026-09-25 final zero-cost gate) as an explicitly authorized human-language-free fork of global_style_v1.json's 'prompt' field, preserving every stated D4 strength (premium Japanese commercial illustration, special-illustration/full-art composition, iconic focal hierarchy, collectible appeal, polished rendering, dynamic depth, strong silhouette/object readability, vivid but controlled color, emotionally engaging atmosphere, high-value finish) while removing every human/character/face/anatomy/pose/gesture word found in the original (expressive faces, bright appealing eyes, elegant stylized anatomy, expressive but mature character design, clean character silhouettes, lively gestures, hypersexualized anime proportions, fan-service pose, and the 'supporting people' focal-hierarchy tier, which is now 'supporting environment or secondary objects'). V1's global_style_v1.json file itself is untouched and remains the sole source for all real V1/production generation.
screen_policy_v2: For any screen or device display that is semantically necessary to this hobby: the screen's content must be abstract, non-readable, non-branded light, color, or texture - never a readable UI, never a wall of code, never a fake dashboard (unless the hobby's identity genuinely requires a dashboard-like readout, in which case keep any numbers/labels abstract and non-legible), and never a human portrait, face thumbnail, social-media profile photo, or video-call participant of any kind, on any screen or poster anywhere in the scene. The screen should visually support the object or system already established as this card's protagonist, never introduce a human subject of its own. Where a screen is not essential to communicating this hobby, avoid a front-facing screen entirely and prefer physical equipment, process, or environment instead.
non_human_protagonist_policy: This artwork must contain ZERO real human presence - no people, no faces, no heads, no hands, no arms, no legs, no feet, no body parts, no human silhouettes, no crowds, no spectators, no players, no workers, no staff, no passersby, no portraits, no photographs of people, no screen images of people, no posters containing people, no reflections containing people, no person-shaped shadows, no cropped humans, and no distant background humans. This rule applies BOTH to the physical scene AND to any media, screen, or display shown inside the scene. Hobby-intrinsic non-real human-LIKE objects are allowed only when unmistakably small physical game pieces with a visible base/stand (tabletop miniatures, chess pieces, figurines) - never a dynamically-posed character with expressive facial detail. Real animals are allowed and encouraged where semantically appropriate (this is a zero-HUMANS rule, not a zero-living-beings rule). STRUCTURAL CONTAINMENT METHOD: do not design a normal human-centered scene and then try to remove the person - design the scene from the start so no human presence is structurally expected, per the matched structural_containment_rules_v2.json rule for this hobby's archetype.
character_substitution_policy: When a human is excluded from this scene, do NOT fill that human's role with a substitute character - no anthropomorphic animals, no mascots, no humanoid robots pretending to be a person, no toy or doll figures acting as full-scale scene participants, and no fantasy creatures performing a human professional or social role (for example, no owl acting as a lawyer or judge, no animal mascot standing in for a courtroom participant). The correct solution is an empty, structurally non-human scene, not a costumed stand-in. This rule does not apply to: a real animal where the animal itself is the genuine subject of the hobby (a zero-HUMANS rule, not a zero-living-beings rule); tabletop miniatures, chess pieces, or figurines that clearly read as small physical objects at miniature scale; statues or figurines that clearly read as objects, not living participants; media/collectible figures (for example anime-culture collectibles) that clearly read as small physical display objects; or a hobby that is specifically and literally about robots, where a robot is the genuine subject rather than a stand-in for a person.
character_substitution_policy_origin: Added after Validation-8 (commit c7d00b9) found learning.mock_trial rendered anthropomorphic owl characters standing in for human courtroom participants - a genuine architecture gap the prior checkpoints had not anticipated: removing humans without this explicit rule left the model free to invent a costumed substitute rather than an empty scene.
human_operated_object_gate_v2: If an action normally requires a human hand or body to perform, do not depict the object actively performing that action by itself unless there is a visible, plausible mechanical support or automation explaining the motion (a motorized device, an automatic machine, gravity, wind, momentum already in progress, or a mechanically supported rig). Never show a kettle pouring by itself, a pen or brush writing or painting by itself, a spoon stirring by itself, scissors cutting by themselves, a microphone floating as if being held, a racket swinging itself, a camera floating as if actively taking a photo, or pages turning as if by an invisible hand. Instead, default to a resting, completed, or paused state: a kettle resting beside a finished coffee setup, a pen resting on a notebook beside already-written pages, a brush resting beside a canvas, scissors resting on a table, a microphone mounted on a stand, a racket resting on a court or bench, a camera mounted on a tripod, pages lying open naturally. Active motion is only allowed when it is physically plausible without a hand: an automated or motorized machine genuinely operating under its own established mechanism, gravity, a motorized device, wind, an object already rolling, bouncing, or falling, liquid settling after a recent disturbance, or motion that is mechanically supported and visibly explained.
human_operated_object_gate_v2_origin: Added after Wave-B-48 (commit 6848b4b) surfaced a repeated cross-hobby pattern - a floating self-pouring kettle (food.coffee), a floating self-writing pen (learning.fiction) - joining the earlier floating-chopsticks and floating-watering-can findings from prior rounds. The existing physical-logic domains only covered specific object categories (utensils, sport tools, instruments); this is a general, catalog-wide gate covering any human-operated object regardless of domain, applied unconditionally alongside the domain-specific physical-logic text rather than as a one-off per-hobby fix.
anti_sameness_policy: Do not default to warm golden-hour light, a centered hero object, a cozy warm interior, or floating sparkle particles as the default treatment. Follow this card's assigned composition_diversity_v2.json routes (composition_archetype, palette_lighting_route, effect_level) exactly.

text_policy_v2.principle: The problem is unwanted/generated nonsense text (fake titles, slogans, labels, UI copy), not text as a concept. Do not return to a blanket 'all text is forbidden' rule.
suppress_when: not semantically important to the hobby
likely to render as a fake label, title, slogan, or UI string
allow_when_semantically_natural: abstract calligraphy brushwork (gestural, not a complete readable word, per the existing arts.calligraphy exception)
tiny non-legible print or notation intrinsic to an object
maps as abstract line/shape work, no readable place names
game board markings (abstract symbols, not a readable title)
sheet-music-like notation (abstract staff/note marks, not readable lyrics)
decorative symbols intrinsic to a craft or culture
text_policy_v2.relationship_to_v1: This mirrors V1's already-validated arts_text_suppression_policy and business_text_suppression_policy approach (suppress unwanted generated text, not text as a concept) rather than introducing a new, stricter regime.

brand_safety_policy_reuse_note: V2 reuses global_style_v1.json's global_brand_safety_policy unchanged (generic/unbranded clothing, footwear, equipment, devices, vehicles; no logos/brand marks/swoosh-like or three-stripe-like marks/sneaker-brand silhouettes). No destructive modification of this validated policy is made or planned by V2.
card_ui_suppression_reuse_note: V2 reuses V1's existing full-bleed / no-card-frame / no-rarity-badge / no-title-panel / no-stats-box / no-TCG-shell / no-watermark suppression language unchanged.
